review_purpose: Review settled R798 knowledge-collection report for scope fit, substantive depth, overlap, source attribution versus independently verified evidence, and section-limited retrieval metadata. Read-only review; the research index was not modified. No source inspection, external-source verification, builds, tests, GPU/profiler work, process inspection, cleanup, Git, environment changes, or worker actions were performed.

research_index_snapshot.note: Read for existing round metadata and prior retrieval boundaries. R798 was not present in the index snapshot. The index remains unchanged.

scope_depth_review: At 1,480 whitespace-delimited words, the report is within the 1,300–1,800-word assignment budget and cites six source families, below the seven-source limit. It covers the requested skinny, ragged-batch, and large dense GEMM regimes; compares regular output-tile ownership, padding, grouped scheduling, and K-splitting countercosts; includes one crossover table and one bounded prospective experiment. It distinguishes reported hardware and precision where known, marks transfer to Xe2/SYCL as hypotheses, and makes no local bottleneck, speed, quality, or adoption claim. This is substantive and coherent without material filler.
novelty_and_redundancy: R798 is distinct from R796's R793 oneDNN API/type and queue contracts and R790's R789 residual mapping/fusion analysis: its unit of comparison is dense GEMM output-tile scheduling across shape regimes. Index metadata identifies R778 as sparse SpMV/SpMM and R779 as irregular gather; those topics are adjacent but not duplicates. R628 is indexed as a GEMM scheduling census and R701 as local grouped-GEMM/prefill work, so topical overlap exists. Their report bodies were not reopened; R798 explicitly avoids inferring local shapes or a local bottleneck. Treat novelty as a useful external geometry-focused archive, not as proven absence of overlap with every older GEMM source. Do not dispatch another general padding/grouping/tile-scheduling survey.
source_precision_and_provenance: The report supplies six traceable citations with URLs, version/date identifiers where available, and SHA-256 values it attributes to retrieved page/PDF bytes: two proceedings papers, two versioned arXiv papers, CUTLASS 4.8.0 documentation, and Intel oneAPI GPU Optimization Guide 2025.2. It gives useful limits, including the cited accumulation uncertainty for the MAGMA study, FP32/FP64-only precision for the TSM2X study, and the specific A100 FP16-input/FP32-accumulation/output setup for Stream-K. This reviewer did not open the external sources or reproduce their hashes; source claims and hashes remain report-attributed, not independently verified here. No source code, helper, test, or implementation proposal is present, so no implementation provenance or license is being asserted. External results and CUDA guidance do not establish Xe2 behavior.
evidence_limits: R798 is a knowledge archive only. Its papers and vendor documentation do not establish a Strata bottleneck, target-device code generation, local tile optimum, model quality, or speedup.
The report's transfer statements are hypotheses. It does not inspect the installed compiler/runtime, XMX lowering, register or SLM use, actual shape distribution, physical traffic, or occupancy.

The source retrieval hashes and literature descriptions were not independently verified during this review; the listed source hardware and arithmetic modes should be treated as report-attributed until a concrete decision requires source inspection.

The report's prospective three-policy experiment is not a qualification gate. Any local result would need an owned fixture and correctness contract, controlled clean-process measurements of the whole dependency path, and the applicable context and retention requirements.
